ArtifactView.description:
One stored file: what the approval view shows beside it (template,
case version, hash), and whether this caller may download it now.
ArtifactView.title: ArtifactView

AuditEventView.description:
One audit row as the screen shows it.

``actor_id`` is here because it was the one thing the table could not show:
the column exists on the row and is not inside ``details``, so dropping it
from this view made "who did this" unanswerable from the UI for every action,
not only sharing (spec 03.1 BR10 names it explicitly).
AuditEventView.title: AuditEventView

CancelResult.description:
Whether a run was actually stopped, not whether the request was understood.

`False` is an ordinary answer: the turn had already finished, or another
process holds it. A caller pressing Stop twice should get 200 both times —
the second one describes a thread that is already not running, which is what
they asked for.
CancelResult.title: CancelResult

CaseChangeView.description: What a mutation answers: which case, at which version, in which state.
CaseChangeView.title: CaseChangeView

CopperBasisView.description: How a price follows copper. A band's limits are prices of copper.
CopperBasisView.title: CopperBasisView

EvidenceView.title: EvidenceView

ExportRow.description:

took a case through it, beside the minutes it takes by hand.
ExportRow.title: ExportRow

FindingCode.description: The order checks of the spec's findings table, one code each.
FindingCode.title: FindingCode

FixedCopper.description: The price does not move with copper.
FixedCopper.title: FixedCopper

FlaggedValue.description: One value read from a flagged region, by the field it fills.

Hidden.description: An amount the caller may not see: there, and not shown.

requires_approval.description: True if this tool always requires approval, at every autonomy level. False does not mean it never pauses: whether a given call does depends on the run.

LabelledAnchor.description: Where one value was read, named by the field (and line) it fills.

OrderSummaryView.description: A row of the order list: no amount at all.

PageBox.description:
A rectangle on a rendered page, as fractions of the page.

``x`` and ``y`` are the top-left corner measured from the page's top-left,
so the box draws the same at any zoom and on any renderer.

``items`` — is the client's stop condition: a filtered listing can return an
empty page in the middle of a run and still have more rows behind it.

Each is a place a person looking at the file would not see the value, or

ScreeningRow.description:

SheetCell.description: One cell as the workbook holds it, with why a person might not see it.

SourceAnchor.description:

At least one of: ``cell_ref`` (``Sheet!B10``), ``page`` with its
``boxes``, or ``quote``, the words as the file prints them. More than one
may be given when the reader knows more than one.

ValueState.description: How sure a value on a case is (CONTEXT.md "Value states").
ValueState.title: ValueState

VersionBody.description: The case version the decision was made on.
VersionBody.title: VersionBody

post.description:
Files the request and flips the tenant to `offboarding` immediately.

202, not 200 or 204: the export/purge itself runs later, on the worker's
offboarding lane — this call only starts it.

The operator's explicit second step, once GET .../offboard reports
`completed` — see ProvisioningService.finalize_offboarding's docstring
for why this is not automatic.

post.description:
Stop the run in flight on this thread.

The runner's own `cancel_thread` takes a thread id and nothing else: it
looks the task up in an in-process dict, which is safe while the only caller
is a run that started it. Over HTTP the id is whatever the caller typed, so
ownership is established HERE, against the database under the caller's
tenant, before the runner is asked to do anything.

A thread this tenant has never run on is a 404 rather than a 403. "Not
yours" and "never existed" are the same answer to someone probing ids, and
the difference between them is exactly what a prober is trying to learn.
